## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kuṇḍadhānattheragāthā* (Thag 1.15) is a single-verse poetic discourse included in the first chapter (ekakanipāta) of the *Theragāthā* within the Pali Canon [Kuṇḍadhānattheragāthā Catalog Record; SuttaCentral]. Attributed to the elder Kuṇḍadhāna, the poem belongs to the earliest stratum of Buddhist verse preserved in the Khuddaka Nikāya [Kuṇḍadhānattheragāthā Catalog Record; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral catalogs nine translations across eight modern languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

The text shares close intertextual links across early Buddhist literature. SuttaCentral identifies a full canonical parallel in verse 370 of the Pali *Dhammapada* (Dhp 370) [SuttaCentral]. Passage-level parallels exist in the Gāndhārī Dharmapada (*G-Dhp* 51–90, *Bhikhuvagga*), the *Katichindasutta* of the Saṃyutta Nikāya (SN 1.5), and the Chinese *Dharmapada* translation (T 210.34, 沙門品法句經第三十四三十有二章) [SuttaCentral]. Furthermore, the verse is cited in the paracanonical treatise *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37, *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna*) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse queries via DharmaNexus identified no additional Pali-internal reuse or cross-language alignments meeting standard similarity thresholds [DharmaNexus].
